title: Descent of the actual inner-support unit on the full root nerve
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a characteristic-$p$ field $k$, a finite norm-topological extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega\supset E$ with its extended norm topology. For $F=E,\Omega$ use $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ with all continuous maps, $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$, internal modules on small pro-etale sites and ordinary unbounded K-injective derived categories [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $B\to Y$ an affine etale chart whose reduced strict normal crossings boundary has precisely the branches $V(t_d)$, $1\le d\le r$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$ be affine pro-etale and put $S=U\times_B V(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$, with inclusion $s:S\hookrightarrow U$. Define
$$\mathcal T=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R[x_{d,n}]_{1\le d\le r}/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_d\right),$$
where the index is positive integers prime to $p$ ordered by divisibility and $x_{d,n}\mapsto x_{d,m}^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$. Let $i:S\to\mathcal T$ set all roots to zero. Partition $\{1,\ldots,r\}=I_o\sqcup I_i$ with $I_i\ne\varnothing$. Put $V=U[1/\prod_{d\in I_o}t_d]$, $W=U[1/\prod_{d=1}^r t_d]$, $a:V\hookrightarrow U$, $b:W\hookrightarrow V$, and let $h:Z\hookrightarrow V$ be the reduced closed complement of $W$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $\mathcal T^\circ=\mathcal T\times_UW$. Specify compatible primitive roots of unity on $U$ identifying its root deck group with $G=G_o\times G_i$, $G_e=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^{I_e}$; the product is over primes and $\mathbf Z_q=\varprojlim_m\mathbf Z/q^m\mathbf Z$. Assume $\mathcal T^\circ\to W$ is a pro-etale $G$-torsor, with its root deck action. For a profinite $P$ write $X[P]=\varprojlim_{P\twoheadrightarrow P_d}\coprod_{P_d}X$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects].
Let $L$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{E,W}$-module and let $\mathcal N$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{E,\mathcal T}$-module with continuous $G$-equivariant structure and a specified equivariant identification $\mathcal N|_{\mathcal T^\circ}\cong L|_{\mathcal T^\circ}$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Specify a $G$-equivariant identification $i^*\mathcal N\cong p_S^*M_E$ for a finite-dimensional norm-topological continuous $E$-representation $M$ of $G$, where $M_F(P)=C(P,F\otimes_E M)$ has the finite-dimensional product norm topology. Put $\mathcal N_F=C_{F,\mathcal T}\otimes_{C_{E,\mathcal T}}\mathcal N$ and $L_F=C_{F,W}\otimes_{C_{E,W}}L$ by ordinary tensor. Actions and derived invariants use [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation, def-sfb-condensed-action-module, def-sfb-norm-continuous-monodromy-data]. Let
$$B_F^n(M)=R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[G^n],M_F)$$
be the inhomogeneous internal derived bar, whose first face acts on $M_F$ and whose other faces multiply or delete coordinates; $C_F[P]$ is the free internal module on the condensed set $Q\mapsto C(Q,P)$, and internal Hom is right adjoint to module tensor, derived in its second variable. All totalizations below use coherent compatible nonnegative resolutions and finite diagonals, rather than an unspecified diagram in a triangulated category.
For $P=G^n$, let $f_n:\mathcal T^\circ[P]\to V$ be structural and put $K_{n,F}=R(f_n)_*(\mathcal N_F|_{\mathcal T^\circ[P]}[0])$. Put $K_F=Rb_*L_F[0]$, and use the actual closed adjunction units $\eta_{h,K_F}$ and $\eta_{h,K_{n,F}}$ [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. The termwise restriction-of-sections maps
$$\alpha_{n,F}:s^*R(af_n)_*(\mathcal N_F|_{\mathcal T^\circ[G^n]}[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}p_S^*B_F^n(M)$$
of [lem-sfb-root-tower-boundary-acyclicity] extend to an isomorphism of coherent augmented cosimplicial derived objects
$$\sigma_{n,F}:s^*Ra_*h_*h^*K_{n,F}\xrightarrow{\sim}p_S^*B_F^n(M)$$
satisfying $\sigma_{n,F}\circ s^*Ra_*(\eta_{h,K_{n,F}})=\alpha_{n,F}$ with the canonical derived composition identifications. Compatibility includes the first action face on whole profinite parameter objects. Under the actual Cech augmentation comparisons there are derived isomorphisms
$$\alpha_F:s^*Ra_*Rb_*L_F[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}p_S^*\operatorname{Tot}B_F^\bullet(M),\quad
\sigma_F:s^*Ra_*h_*h^*Rb_*L_F[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}p_S^*\operatorname{Tot}B_F^\bullet(M)$$
with $\sigma_F\circ s^*Ra_*(\eta_{h,K_F})=\alpha_F$. Thus the same coherent bar is used on both sides, with its specified augmentation, not independently chosen isomorphic objects. Here $Z$ is the union of the inner zero loci in $V$; the support functor is applied after $R(f_n)_*$ on $V$. The constructions are natural in maps of supplied equivariant extensions and pro-etale restrictions of $U$. They hold separately for both $F$ with the same root data, include $I_o=\varnothing$, zero modules and empty charts, and make no claim about arbitrary unbounded product totalizations or preservation of injectives by $h^*$. If $W=U\times_YW_0$ and $V=U\times_YV_0$ for open immersions $b_0:W_0\hookrightarrow V_0$ and $j_0:V_0\hookrightarrow Y$, with reduced closed complement $h_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow V_0$, and $L$ is the restriction of a module $L_0$ on $W_0$, the displayed unit diagram is the slice restriction along $U\to Y$ of $Rj_{0,*}(\eta_{h_0,Rb_{0,*}L_{0,F}[0]})$, followed by $s^*$. Coefficient rings in the slices are the pulled-back rings, and this compatibility is for the actual global unit, not a newly chosen adjunction on a slice.

proof.text:
Fix $F$ and use the supplied extension on the full tower. Its ordinary scalar extension is lisse: on a pro-etale slice trivializing $\mathcal N$ as $C_E^m$, its tensor with $C_F$ is $C_F^m$. Exact inverse image and its monoidal coefficient identifications give the boundary model $p_S^*M_F$; here $F\otimes_E M$ is finite free and its continuous functions are the corresponding finite product of $C_F$. The equivariant boundary identification transports the supplied deck action to the specified action on $M_F$. Apply boundary acyclicity and the one-term inner-support theorem to this same extension with $P=G^n$. Their schemes $U,S,T,V,W$, partition and maps are exactly those in the statement. We obtain the specified $\alpha_{n,F}$, the isomorphism $\sigma_{n,F}$, and
$$\sigma_{n,F}\,s^*Ra_*(\eta_{h,K_{n,F}})=\alpha_{n,F}.$$
The latter theorem applies support after the structural direct image on $V$, and treats the reduced union of inner zero loci, including non-singleton $I_i$; we do not replace it by one branch.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: apply the existing one-term comparisons on the supplied common chart

proof.text: Use the assumed torsor identification to label an $(n+1)$-tuple of vertices by its first vertex and its successive deck increments. The torsor identity $T^\circ[G]\cong T^\circ\times_WT^\circ$ iterates to $T^\circ[G^n]$: the vertices are $x,xg_1,xg_1g_2,\ldots,xg_1\cdots g_n$, with the deck/descent convention chosen for the given equivariant pullback of $L$. Deleting an interior vertex multiplies its adjacent increments, deleting the last removes the last increment, and repeating a vertex inserts the identity. Deleting vertex zero changes the base vertex by $g_1$ and hence acts on the coefficient by its supplied descent action. These assertions follow by substituting the displayed vertices; they are scheme maps on the profinite parameter objects by the torsor isomorphism, not just formulas on geometric points. Thus these are exactly the inhomogeneous bar operators. Parameter naturality of both comparisons in step 1 handles multiplication, deletion and identity insertion. For the first face use their family clauses with parameter $Q=G$: its base-vertex move is the entire $G$-family of root deck automorphisms, whose boundary action is $M_F$ by the equivariant identification. Consequently both comparisons commute with this face on the whole family. The cosimplicial identities are inherited from vertex deletion and repetition, and the termwise unit equality commutes with every operator by naturality of the actual unit.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: check all faces, degeneracies and the first action face on whole profinite parameters

proof.text: Present the covering $T^\circ\to W$ by its representable epimorphism on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Its Cech slices are the small pro-etale sites of the iterated fibre products, hence of $T^\circ[G^n]$ in step 2; clause (1) of weakly etale localization supplies this site identification. Rings are always restricted pulled-back rings. The open/closed theorem gives exact $h^*,h_*$ and their specified unit. Apply closed-unit Cech totalization with $\mathcal X=W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $f=b$, $g=a$, $t=s$, $N=L_F$ and this cover. The pullback of $L_F$ on each nerve term is the specified restriction of $\mathcal N_F$. Therefore its $C_n$ is $K_{n,F}$. We get augmentation-preserving isomorphisms from $s^*Ra_*Rb_*L_F[0]$ and $s^*Ra_*h_*h^*Rb_*L_F[0]$ to the respective totals of the two term diagrams in step 1. Under them the actual map $s^*Ra_*(\eta_{h,K_F})$ is the totalized termwise unit. All sites and the countable Cech diagram are small in the coefficient universes. Normalize $R(af_n)_*\cong Ra_*R(f_n)_*$ by the conjugate of inverse-image composition, so it preserves these adjunction units.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: apply Cech descent to both diagrams and to the actual closed unit

proof.text: Use coherent nonnegative resolutions retaining the maps of the augmented diagrams in steps 1--3, as in nonnegative derived totalization. On these models the horizontal differential is the alternating sum of the cofaces of step 2 and the total differential is $d_{\rm Cech}+(-1)^n d_{\rm res}$. In total degree $r$ there are only pairs $n,q\geq0$ with $n+q=r$ (or triples if a further replacement is made), hence finite diagonals. The comparison theorem is natural for augmented diagram maps and independent of the compatible resolutions. Thus the comparisons of step 2 retain their coherent augmentation when totalized; they are not a total assigned to bare objects in a triangulated category. Exact $p_S^*$ commutes with these finite diagonals. The termwise comparison isomorphisms give isomorphisms of totals: filter the cone total by Cech degree; in each fixed total degree the filtration is finite, and its column cohomology is zero. Composing these totals with step 3 defines $\alpha_F$ and $\sigma_F$ with common target $p_S^*\operatorname{Tot}B_F^\bullet(M)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: retain compatible nonnegative resolutions and their augmentations

proof.text:
Totalize the equality in step 1 using the same resolutions on its commuting diagram. Step 3 identifies the totalized middle arrow with the actual unit after $Ra_*$ and $s^*$, and step 4 identifies the outer maps with $\sigma_F,\alpha_F$. Functoriality of totalization gives
$$\sigma_F\,s^*Ra_*(\eta_{h,K_F})=\alpha_F.$$
In particular this equality uses one bar and its given augmentation. It does not select two unrelated isomorphisms to that bar.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: compose the commuting augmented diagrams

proof.text: Maps of supplied equivariant extensions commute with the term comparisons by their naturality; the family clause in step 2 makes them maps of the same bar diagrams. Pro-etale restriction of $U$ has this property as well. The Cech theorem preserves these maps and refinements, and the nonnegative comparison preserves augmentations. Therefore the constructed $\alpha,\sigma$ and unit equality are natural in exactly the asserted maps. Perform the construction separately for $E$ and $\Omega$ on the same supplied tower; no scalar/direct-image isomorphism is used. If $I_o$ is empty then $a$ is the identity and $G_o$ is trivial; the one-term and Cech theorems still apply. Rank zero gives zero diagrams. An empty chart or empty $S$ gives zero after $s^*$, so all assertions remain valid. No infinite product totalization or preservation of injectives by $h^*$ is invoked.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: naturality, the two coefficient fields and small cases

proof.text: For the final global clause, $U\to Y$ is pro-etale (affine pro-etale over an etale chart), hence gives a slice of the small site. Weakly etale localization, clause (1), identifies that slice with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and the analogous source slices with $V,W,Z$. Apply the ringed-topos sheaf-slice derived comparison to $j_0,b_0,h_0$ with this target sheaf. Its direct-image comparison is represented on K-injectives by the ordinary restriction/direct-image identity, and its inverse-image comparison is the canonical one. Its assertion that these are adjunction mates identifies the units as well as the counits: both proposed unit arrows transpose to the identity of the restricted inverse image, so the adjunction hom bijection makes them equal. For $h_0$, exactness of closed direct image identifies its derived functor with $h_{0,*}$ and likewise on the slice. Consequently the local $\eta_{h,K_F}$ is the restriction of $\eta_{h_0,Rb_{0,*}L_{0,F}[0]}$, after the $b_0$ comparison. Apply the $j_0$ comparison and then $s^*$ to obtain precisely the final unit diagram in the statement. This argument uses pulled-back rings throughout and never equips an arbitrary sliced additive functor with a newly chosen adjunction.
